executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with zoonotic spillover risk, dengue and chikungunya arboviral circulation at elevated levels, and resurgent pertussis across the Western Hemisphere. Mpox continues to circulate in the Americas region while seasonal influenza transitions mark dual hemispheric risk windows. ECDC weekly threat reports spanning Weeks 16-20 of 2026 indicate sustained European communicable disease monitoring activity requiring continued vigilance.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous biological threats—including H5N1 avian influenza with pandemic potential, record arboviral transmission, and resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases—are active across the Americas and Europe, demanding coordinated cross-border surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from animal reservoirs with pandemic potential
Dual animal and human surveillance alerts issued within 4-month window suggesting escalating geographic spread
threats.action: Immediate enhancement of animal-human interface surveillance, veterinary and public health coordination, and pre-pandemic H5N1 vaccine stockpile review

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Historically high arboviral burden in Americas coinciding with chikungunya co-circulation
Seasonal amplification expected during Southern Hemisphere winter travel period
threats.action: Strengthen vector control operations, enhance case-based surveillance, and issue travel health advisories for affected countries

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Viruses
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses, Respiratory Syncytial Virus
threats.location: Americas Region (Northern and Southern Hemispheres), Europe
signals: PAHO alert for simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation issued January 2026
Southern Hemisphere 2026 season start alert issued April 2026
ECDC weekly threat reports Weeks 16-20 of 2026 indicating ongoing European respiratory virus monitoring
Back-to-back hemispheric season transitions create continuous global risk window
threats.action: Accelerate Southern Hemisphere influenza vaccination campaigns, monitor ICU capacity, and track antigenic match between circulating strains and vaccine composition

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing regional circulation
Sustained transmission beyond initial outbreak period indicates endemic establishment risk
Concurrent ECDC monitoring in Europe suggests intercontinental linkage
threats.action: Expand mpox vaccination coverage among high-risk populations, reinforce contact tracing capacity, and harmonize case definitions across member states

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating persistent resurgence
Multi-month sustained alert cycle suggests waning vaccine immunity and coverage gaps driving transmission
Dual alerts within 4-month interval indicate failure to contain initial wave
threats.action: Audit national immunization coverage data, implement catch-up vaccination campaigns, and issue clinical guidance for early case identification and treatment

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue strains vector control resources and complicates clinical diagnosis
Alert timing suggests early 2026 seasonal uptick preceding peak transmission period
threats.action: Implement integrated Aedes vector control, enhance differential diagnosis capacity in clinical settings, and monitor for geographic expansion into previously unaffected areas

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active risk
Vaccination coverage gaps in endemic zones create conditions for urban transmission spillover
Epizootic activity in non-human primate populations typically precedes human cases
threats.action: Verify yellow fever vaccination coverage in at-risk populations, strengthen epizootics surveillance in sylvatic zones, and enforce vaccination requirements for travelers

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 signaling reintroduction or resurgence risk
Americas had achieved measles elimination status making any re-emergence a significant public health regression
Concurrent pertussis resurgence suggests broader vaccine-preventable disease immunity gaps in the region
threats.action: Conduct rapid subnational vaccination coverage assessments, strengthen outbreak response capacity, and ensure surveillance sensitivity can detect imported cases

amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis resurgence with dual alerts within 4 months may reflect macrolide resistance or treatment failure warranting antimicrobial susceptibility surveillance
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (Report 12) may indicate counterfeit pharmaceutical supply chains that could co-distribute antimicrobial-resistant contaminants
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory threat convergence (H5N1, seasonal influenza, RSV) across both hemispheres creates compounding diagnostic and healthcare capacity challenges
Resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) concurrent with arboviral expansion suggests systemic immunization program disruption likely linked to COVID-19 pandemic recovery gaps

Dual H5N1 animal surveillance alerts within a 4-month window (November 2025, March 2026) suggests expanding geographic footprint of highly pathogenic avian influenza with increased zoonotic interface events
Back-to-back PAHO arboviral alerts (dengue February, chikungunya February, yellow fever March 2026) indicate a broad Aedes-driven transmission surge across the Americas in early 2026

ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly communicable disease threat reports (Weeks 16-20, 2026) indicates an unusually active multi-threat European surveillance period requiring intercontinental coordination
